findings.title: Lint/type debt is a global ratchet, never diff-scoped, never required to shrink
findings.principle: Every PR's lint and type check runs twice: once as the existing repo-wide ratchet (must not exceed the current baseline), and once scoped ONLY to lines changed in that PR (via git diff against the merge-base), where the changed-lines pass must be zero-error for @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any, no-unused-vars, and no-html-link-for-pages, with no baseline exception. Separately, the repo-wide lint baseline (currently frozen at 481 since the gate was created) is lowered by a fixed amount on a fixed cadence (for example 20 errors per calendar month) until it reaches 0; a month where it does not move is logged as its own entry in _tasks/INCOMPLETE_FEATURES.md.
findings.why: A global ratchet only guarantees the total count never goes up. It does not guarantee that NEW code is clean, because a PR can add 5 new `any`s in file A while an unrelated PR removes 5 in file B, and both individually pass. That laundering is exactly why the baseline has not moved since it was set. Without a diff-scoped floor, 'any' discipline exists only on paper: the rule is already configured as an ESLint ERROR (verified below), so the gap is not the rule text, it is that nothing stops the count from staying frozen forever.
findings.local_evidence: next.config.mjs:9 sets eslint.ignoreDuringBuilds:true (lint never blocks a production build) while typescript.ignoreBuildErrors:false (type errors do). .github/workflows/quality.yml's lint job compares npm run lint output against BASELINE=481 and only fails if the count goes UP; git log -p shows this baseline was set once (commit ed5cf0557) and never lowered since, while the sibling tsc ratchet in the same file WAS driven from BASELINE=5 to BASELINE=0 in a later commit (53c1890ea) -- proving the team can do a real paydown when it decides to, it just never scheduled one for lint. A live `npm run lint` run (1209 output lines) breaks down as: 354 @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any (classified as Error), 64 no-html-link-for-pages (Error -- real internal <a> tags to /privacy/, /datenschutz/, / that force full page reloads instead of Next.js client navigation), 55 no-unescaped-entities (Error), 210 @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars (Warning), 16 no-img-element (Warning, bypasses next/image). Separately, `as any` appears 338 times and bare `!.` non-null assertions ~31 times across app/components/lib. No husky, lint-staged, or .git/hooks/pre-commit exists, and no .claude hook targets `any` or unused-var introduction at write time.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rn 'diff.*scope\|new.code.*gate\|changed.lines\|only.*changed.files' _design-system _docs _rules CLAUDE.md .github/workflows -> no hits describing a diff-scoped lint/type gate. grep -n 'BASELINE' .github/workflows/quality.yml shows two static integers (0 for tsc, 481 for lint) with no schedule to lower either. ls .husky, grep -n 'husky\|lint-staged' package.json, find . -maxdepth 1 -iname '.pre-commit*' all returned nothing.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: quality.yml already prevents lint/tsc regressions from getting WORSE (a real, working floor). It does not cover: (a) diff-scoped enforcement so new code can't launder against old debt, (b) any mechanism or schedule to pay the 481 down.
findings.where_it_should_live: .github/workflows/quality.yml (add a diff-scoped job) + a new _rules/LINT_DEBT.md tracking the paydown schedule
findings.enforcement: gate: a new CI job running eslint against `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` with --max-warnings=0 for the three named rules; the paydown schedule is a checklist, not a gate (advisory, checked monthly)

findings.title: No component-level error boundary; a single client widget's render crash can take down the whole route
findings.principle: Any client component whose render depends on data it fetched itself (currently 171 files match useEffect+fetch) is wrapped in a React error boundary (class component with getDerivedStateFromError, or a small shared <SectionErrorBoundary> built on the existing ErrorState primitive) that catches render-time exceptions locally and shows <ErrorState onRetry> for that section only, so a malformed API response in one widget never blanks the rest of the page. Every top-level route segment additionally gets its own error.tsx (Next.js route-level boundary), starting with every segment on a money path (booking, walk-in, tip) that does not have one yet.
findings.why: Next.js's own error.tsx only catches errors thrown during a route segment's render; it does not isolate one client component's exception from its siblings on the same page, so a bad review, a null salon photo array, or an unexpected API shape inside any ONE of the PDP's ~15 sibling sections (SalonReviews, SalonTeam, SalonServices, etc.) can currently propagate up and white-screen the entire salon page instead of degrading just that section.
findings.local_evidence: grep -rln 'componentDidCatch\|getDerivedStateFromError' across app, components, components-legacy, lib returned ZERO files -- there is no React error boundary class anywhere in the codebase. `find app -name error.tsx` returns exactly 10 files, but `find "app/[locale]" -maxdepth 1 -type d` shows 56 top-level route segments (barbershop, coiffeur, nails, spa, search, inspo, booking, bookings, dashboard, profile, salon, walk-in-pay, walk-in-tip, tip, queue, confirmation, etc.) -- meaning 46 of 56 top-level segments have no error.tsx of their own and would surface at the nearest ancestor boundary (or the root app/error.tsx) instead of a scoped one. 171 files combine useEffect with fetch(, i.e. render client-side off data that can arrive malformed.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rln 'ErrorBoundary' app components components-legacy lib -> 0 hits (the only 'ErrorFallback' hits are the route-level components-legacy/ui/ErrorFallback.tsx and the 10 error.tsx files that import it, not a reusable in-tree boundary). grep -n 'react-error-boundary' package.json -> no hits (package not installed).
findings.existing_coverage: partial: COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md documents ErrorState (inline, for a panel whose fetch failed) and ErrorFallback ({error, reset}, for route-level error.tsx) as locked primitives, and says to pair them so a dashboard panel 'never shows an indefinite spinner.' Neither primitive is wired into an actual React error boundary that catches an unhandled render exception -- they only cover the case where the CALLER manually catches a fetch failure and conditionally renders ErrorState; a thrown exception during render (e.g. calling .map on an unexpectedly-null field) is not caught by either today.
findings.where_it_should_live: a new primitives/SectionErrorBoundary.tsx entry in COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md, wired around the highest-risk client sections first (booking wizard steps, PDP sections, dashboard panels)
findings.enforcement: checklist item in the section-build checklist (STRUCTURAL_RULES.md Rule 46 pre-commit checklist) today; could graduate to a lint rule (react/no-unstable-nested-components-style custom rule) once the boundary component exists

findings.title: No state-ownership doctrine (URL vs server props vs Context vs local); the tree is 37% client-rendered with 171 files fetching client-side
findings.principle: State picks exactly one owner, in this priority order: (1) anything that should be shareable, back-button-safe, or survive a refresh (a filter, an active tab, a search query, a selected date) lives in the URL via searchParams, never in component state; (2) anything known at request time and not re-computed per-interaction is fetched once in the nearest Server Component and passed down as a prop, never re-fetched client-side with useEffect; (3) anything shared by more than two sibling client components on one page lives in a single page-scoped Context/reducer (the existing BookingProvider pattern), never duplicated per component; (4) everything else is local useState. A new client component that calls fetch() inside useEffect for data that was already available on the server at request time is a violation unless the file states why (e.g. it genuinely depends on a client-only value like geolocation or a just-completed client action).
findings.why: Without a stated ownership order, each new surface re-derives the same fetch/loading/error boilerplate independently (171 separate implementations), duplicates the same data across sibling components instead of sharing one fetch, and drifts further client-side over time because nothing tells a new agent that server-fetch-then-pass-as-props is the default, not the exception, this is a Next.js App Router product.
findings.local_evidence: 296 of 799 .ts/.tsx files under app/ contain "use client" (37%); 175 of 197 files under components/+components-legacy/ do too. 171 files combine useEffect with fetch( for client-side data loading, against a total of only 190 files that call fetch( anywhere -- i.e. almost every fetch call in the whole tree is a client-side one, not a server-fetched prop. This directly contradicts the project's own Rule 42 template (_rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md) which states new feature pages should have 'app/[locale]/[feature]/page.tsx <- Server Component (data fetching)' feeding a client component for interactivity only -- a pattern the salon PDP and booking-wizard shell DO follow (_docs/FRONTEND.md documents both as RSC-fetch-then-pass-props) but which is evidently the minority pattern once you count the whole tree.
findings.absence_proof: grep -in 'state ownership\|source of truth for state\|url state' _design-system/SOURCE.md _docs/FRONTEND.md -> 0 hits. STRUCTURAL_RULES.md Rule 42 states the RSC-fetch pattern as the template for a BRAND NEW feature page only; it is never generalized into a standing rule for existing surfaces, and nothing in CLAUDE.md's precedence-1-8 layer states a state-ownership order.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: Rule 42's file-tree template implies server-fetch-then-client-render for new pages, and the booking flow's BookingProvider is a real, working example of page-scoped Context for shared state. Neither is generalized into a rule that a new PR can be graded against, and there is no URL-vs-Context-vs-local decision tree anywhere.
findings.where_it_should_live: _docs/FRONTEND.md (new short section) or _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md as a new numbered rule
findings.enforcement: checklist item today; could become a custom eslint rule flagging useEffect+fetch in a client component whose parent is already a Server Component with access to the same data

findings.title: No automated duplication detector, despite a documented multi-year history of shipped duplicate components
findings.principle: A structural code-duplication scan (for example jscpd over app/ and components*/, flagging blocks of roughly 30+ duplicated lines or 15+ duplicated tokens) runs in CI alongside the existing design-token drift-checker, and a PR that introduces a block already duplicated 3 or more times elsewhere in the tree fails the same way a hex-color or spacing drift does today. This targets LOGIC/JSX duplication, which is a distinct failure mode from the token-level drift the existing solen-drift-check already catches.
findings.why: The registry itself is the evidence that manual review alone does not catch this class of bug reliably or quickly: real duplicate components shipped and lived in production for extended periods before being found, each time by a human doing a dedicated sweep rather than a running check. A repo this size (203 page routes, 357 API routes) will keep generating this pattern faster than manual sweeps can find it, especially across sub-agent sessions that don't share working memory.
findings.local_evidence: COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md itself documents at least 5 confirmed historical duplication incidents found only by manual sweep: PriceFrom collapsed 3 'ab X CHF' spellings (2 more leftover duplicates found afterward, still unmigrated); SeeAllButton collapsed '4 hand-rolled Alle-ansehen dialects', 3 of which had independently converged on an identical class string; Avatar collapsed '6+ photo-or-initial blocks' plus a '3x copy-pasted staff badge', and a 7th hand-rolled duplicate (profile/page.tsx:235) was found unmigrated during a later re-verification pass; RatingStars collapsed '~14 hand-rolled star+decimal blocks + 5 raw <svg><polygon> five-star renders'; _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md Rule 44 records the historical FilterBar naming collision (287-line old file vs a new file of the same name) that caused import ambiguity. None of these were caught by a running tool; all were found by a human doing a dedicated pass.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'jscpd\|knip\|depcheck\|unimported\|ts-prune\|duplicate' package.json -> no dedup/dead-export tooling installed. `npm run` script list has no duplication-scan script (only inventory, exists, health, check:invariants, check:floors, check:motion, removed, smoke, e2e). The existing solen-drift-check skill/gate is confirmed (by its own description and _design-system/_drift-report.md) to catch hardcoded hex/spacing/duration/token drift only, never logic or JSX-shape duplication.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the design-token drift-checker (solen-drift-check) is a strong, wired gate for a DIFFERENT kind of duplication (visual-token drift). It has no logic/JSX overlap with what jscpd-class tooling would catch.
findings.where_it_should_live: package.json (new devDependency + script) + .github/workflows/quality.yml (new job) or .claude/hooks (PreToolUse gate)
findings.enforcement: gate: CI job on push/PR, mirroring the existing quality.yml lint/tsc jobs' ratchet pattern (start at whatever the current duplication count is, block increases)

findings.title: No file-size / component-size ceiling anywhere in the system
findings.principle: A page or component file exceeding 400 lines must either be split into named sub-components with single responsibilities, or the file's top comment must name why it stays one file (e.g. 'this composes N tightly-coupled layout regions that share local state X'). Files exceeding 800 lines are logged in _tasks/INCOMPLETE_FEATURES.md as decomposition debt with an owner, the same way any other incomplete-feature gap is tracked today.
findings.why: A single file with no size ceiling accumulates responsibilities indefinitely because nothing ever forces a stopping point; the largest files in this codebase are 3-6x the size of the next tier down, which is the classic shape of a component that started focused and had every subsequent feature bolted onto the same file instead of decomposed, making it progressively harder for any single agent (with a bounded context window) to safely edit without regressions.
findings.local_evidence: `wc -l` across all app+components+components-legacy .tsx files, sorted descending: app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchTemplate.tsx = 2375 lines, app/[locale]/dashboard/settings/page.tsx = 1578, app/[locale]/dev/primitives/page.tsx = 1299, app/[locale]/dashboard/calendar/page.tsx = 1154, app/[locale]/_components/search/SearchOverlay.tsx = 1125, components-legacy/refund/RefundCaseView.tsx = 958, app/[locale]/_components/salon/SalonLocation.tsx = 956, app/[locale]/_components/layout/Header.tsx = 891, components-legacy/refund/UpchargeApproveView.tsx = 833, app/[locale]/_components/primitives/DateTimePicker.tsx = 820.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'max.*lines\|file size\|line limit\|too large\|god component\|god file' _design-system _docs _rules CLAUDE.md -> zero hits describing any file-size ceiling; the only 'max-lines' hits found (_design-system/_video-audit/AUDIT.md, LOCKFILE content-resilience row) refer to TEXT truncation (max lines of visible copy in a UI element), not source-file line count.
findings.enforcement: checklist today; could become a gate: a simple `wc -l` check in a PreToolUse hook or CI step that warns (not blocks, given the existing 10 outliers) above 800 lines

findings.title: COMPONENT_REGISTRY has no graduation or retirement threshold; 'live' status has been granted on unverified claims at least 4 times
findings.principle: A component enters the registry as `proposed`, moves to `wip` once built, and only reaches `locked`/`live` when a real import grep (not an agent's unverified claim) shows 2 or more genuine external call-sites -- the exact grep command and its output are pasted into the registry row at promotion time. In the other direction, a `live` component that drops to 0 real call-sites for 2 consecutive registry audits (roughly 60 days, matching the existing audit cadence) is marked `deprecated: <date>, 0 call-sites` and deleted (code + row) 60 days later unless an owner adds a `KEEP: <reason>` note naming a concrete future call-site.
findings.why: A registry whose promotion criterion is an agent's assertion rather than a grep-verified count will keep drifting false, because nothing structurally prevents a wrong claim from being written down as fact and then trusted by the next agent, and once the doc says 'live, N call-sites' the next reader has no reason to re-check it themselves.
findings.local_evidence: The registry's own text documents at least 6 instances where a previously-claimed 'live' call-site count was found FALSE on later re-verification, each labeled 'round-2 correction (2026-07-12)': Modal ('the original 8 dashboard call-sites claim was false', corrected to 2 real ones), Sheet ('dashboard/bookings/page.tsx was falsely claimed before'), Switch ('CityTopBar.tsx was falsely claimed before... it only has an unrelated copy string'), PillToggle ('the 1 real call-site claim was false... 0 real external call-sites found... candidate for retirement, owner call'), Checkbox ('the only used inside PillToggle.tsx claim was false... 0 real external call-sites'), FieldHelper ('the used inside TextInput.tsx claim was false... 0 real external call-sites'). Select, Radio, and Textarea are separately documented as '0 real external call-sites found in this pass' and simply left at status 'live' with no expiry.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'deprecated\|retire\|graduat' _design-system/COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md -> the word 'candidate for retirement' appears exactly once (PillToggle row, an ad hoc note, not a status value); the registry's own 'Status' legend (lines 13-16) defines only locked / wip / proposed, no deprecated/retiring state and no numeric threshold for either direction.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: the registry DOES get periodically re-verified (the 2026-07-12 'A3 registry audit' pass), which is the right instinct, but the audit's findings (0-call-site components) were logged as prose notes rather than triggering an actual status change or deletion clock.
findings.enforcement: checklist today (manual audit); could become a gate: a script that greps each registry entry's file basename against app/+components*/ and diffs against the row's claimed call-site count, failing CI on mismatch

findings.title: components-legacy has confirmed zero-importer dead code with no scheduled sweep; cleanup is reactive and irregular
findings.principle: The orphan-detection loop already written in _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md Rule 40 (bash loop grepping for zero-importer components) runs as a scheduled CI job monthly against BOTH components/ and components-legacy/, not only as a snippet a human might paste in manually. Any file with zero real importers across 2 consecutive monthly runs is auto-listed in a generated _design-system/ORPHAN_REPORT.md and must be either deleted with a REMOVED.md line, or given a one-line `// KEEP: <reason>` comment at the top of the file naming a concrete reason it stays.
findings.why: components-legacy is explicitly named 'legacy' yet has no cadence forcing its dead weight out; every deletion found in REMOVED.md so far happened via an irregularly-named manual pass ('ring 4b', 'ring 10', 'loop iter4', 'SWEEP_BACKLOG'), meaning the folder only shrinks when an agent happens to go looking, and grows continuously in between because normal feature work adds to components-legacy (it is still the live import target for booking, error UI, and more) without a matching removal cadence.
findings.local_evidence: A corrected zero-importer sweep (basename grep against app+components+components-legacy+lib, verified on 5 samples with a direct import-only grep after an initial script bug was caught and fixed) found 17 of 190 components-legacy files with literally zero mentions anywhere outside their own file: components-legacy/ui/beauty-icons.tsx, ScrollableFilterRow.tsx, GlassModal.tsx, components-legacy/home/SectionCarousel.tsx, components-legacy/salon/ServiceCategoryFilter.tsx, components-legacy/search/SearchResultGrid.tsx, MobileViewToggle.tsx, SearchCriteriaChips.tsx, components-legacy/coiffeur/AiMatcherModal.tsx, components-legacy/nail/AllergyWarning.tsx, MaterialSelector.tsx, InspoUploader.tsx, ShapeLengthPicker.tsx, and all 4 files under components-legacy/icons/category/ (BarberIcon, SpaIcon, CoiffeurIcon, NailsIcon). _design-system/REMOVED.md already records at least 9 separate components-legacy deletion waves (angebote/LastMinuteCard, packages-code, compare, makeup/waxing, TestimonialCarousel, ProfilePage 1089 lines, CategoryPage 666 lines, FeaturedSalonCarousel, chat/*, nail/NailBookingSteps+NailsSections, barber/ExpressRebook+RemoteQueueJoin+WaitTimeDisplay, dashboard/LastMinuteManager), each dated months apart with no fixed interval between them.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'monthly\|quarterly\|scheduled sweep\|cadence' _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md CLAUDE.md -> Rule 40's verification command is presented as a manual snippet ('Verification command:') with no cron/CI wiring; grep of .github/workflows/ for any orphan-detection job -> none of the 5 workflow files (inventory-freshness, cron-jobs, db-migrate, invariants, quality) run Rule 40's loop or anything equivalent.
findings.existing_coverage: partial: Rule 40 (STRUCTURAL_RULES.md) already writes the correct detection LOGIC and REMOVED.md already provides the correct RECORD-KEEPING format once a deletion happens. The missing piece is purely cadence: nothing schedules the detection to run periodically instead of only when an agent chooses to run it.
findings.where_it_should_live: .github/workflows/ (new scheduled workflow, e.g. monthly cron) writing to _design-system/ORPHAN_REPORT.md
findings.enforcement: gate: scheduled CI job (cron), not blocking any PR, just surfacing a report; escalates to a real gate only if the report is ignored for 2+ cycles

findings.title: No prop-count ceiling or composition-vs-flat-props guidance for shared component APIs
findings.principle: A component's prop interface exceeding roughly 10 named props (excluding a passthrough `...rest` for native HTML attributes) is a signal to decompose before adding an 11th: either group related props into a single config object, or split the component into a composed set (a base + variant-specific wrapper, or children slots replacing several content-shaped props). DateTimePicker.tsx (17 top-level props on its main export, plus a second exported DateTimePickerRange component living in the same file) is the concrete reference case for when this rule is written.
findings.why: Without a stated ceiling, a shared primitive's prop list only ever grows (each new call-site's need becomes one more optional prop) because nothing prompts a decomposition decision; a 17-prop interface is already hard to reason about for a new agent picking up the file cold, and the failure mode compounds because DateTimePicker is explicitly the ONE locked date/time primitive (V3-D445) that every future date/time surface is required to extend rather than fork, so its prop surface only grows over time.
findings.local_evidence: app/[locale]/_components/primitives/DateTimePicker.tsx's exported DateTimePickerProps interface (lines ~93-132) lists 17 distinct props: value, onChange, slots, isLoadingSlots, minDate, maxDate, isDateDisabled, variant, selectedTone, dateLayout, stripDays, labels, emptySlotContent, dateLabel, timeLabel, className, plus a nested DayStripProps interface further down the same 820-line file for the DateTimePickerRange variant documented in COMPONENT_REGISTRY.md.
findings.absence_proof: grep -rin 'prop explosion\|too many props\|max props\|prop count' _design-system _docs _rules CLAUDE.md -> zero hits. The Universal-components rule (V3-D205, well covered elsewhere) governs a DIFFERENT axis (no category-branching inside a component), not prop-count discipline.
findings.enforcement: checklist item; a custom eslint rule (max-props, not in the default next/typescript preset) could enforce a numeric ceiling once agreed

findings.title: No bundle-size budget or dynamic-import trigger; the practice exists (7 files) with no stated threshold for when it is required
findings.principle: At current pre-launch scale (about 28 salons), a formal bundle budget is premature machinery; the trigger for adopting one is measurable and explicit: wire @next/bundle-analyzer and make next/dynamic (with ssr:false where the content isn't needed for SEO) MANDATORY for any component not needed at first paint (a map, a chart library, a rich editor, an admin-only panel) once EITHER any customer route's First Load JS exceeds 200KB gzipped, OR Lighthouse mobile performance drops below the 70 floor _rules/CODE_SAFETY.md Rule 14 already cites. Until either threshold is crossed, the current ad hoc use of next/dynamic (7 files) is acceptable and does not need to become a blanket policy.
findings.why: Bundle budgets and dynamic-import policies are classic big-company machinery that is genuinely premature at 28 salons and pre-launch traffic; the risk of adopting heavyweight perf tooling now is spending build/CI time on a problem that isn't biting yet, which the SCALE DISCIPLINE constraint explicitly warns against. The finding is not 'add a bundle budget now' -- it is that no measurable trigger is written down anywhere, so nobody will notice when the threshold IS crossed, because nothing is currently measuring First Load JS at all.
findings.local_evidence: grep for 'next/dynamic' across app/ finds exactly 7 files using it (inspo/page.tsx, SalonDetailV3.tsx, SearchOverlay.tsx, SearchTemplate.tsx, dev/pdp/_overhaul/PdpOverhaul.tsx, dev/pdp/portfolio/page.tsx), applied opportunistically rather than against a stated rule. next.config.mjs's experimental.optimizePackageImports covers only lucide-react (with a code comment explaining the historical @phosphor-icons/react removal), no other heavy dependency. No @next/bundle-analyzer or equivalent appears in package.json, so First Load JS per route is not currently measured at all, meaning the trigger this principle proposes cannot even be checked today.
findings.absence_proof: grep -n 'bundle-analyzer\|@next/bundle-analyzer' package.json -> no hits. grep -rin 'bundle size\|bundle budget\|first load js' _design-system _docs _rules CLAUDE.md -> zero hits.
findings.where_it_should_live: _rules/STRUCTURAL_RULES.md or a new _rules/PERFORMANCE.md, once the trigger is crossed
findings.enforcement: doc-only until the named trigger fires; then a CI budget check (Next.js's own build output already reports First Load JS per route, so no new tooling is even required to start watching it)
